overview: Tanzania is a country in East Africa, on the Indian Ocean. Its official capital is Dodoma, while Dar es Salaam is its largest city. Tanzania was formed in 1964 when Tanganyika and the islands of Zanzibar united. Swahili is the national language, and the country is famous for safaris in the Serengeti.

geography.text: Tanzania is home to Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa, and borders three of Africa's largest lakes: Victoria, Tanganyika and Malawi. Much of the country is a high plateau of savanna crossed by the Great Rift Valley, and the Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Crater are famous for their wildlife.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical on the coast, cooler in the highlands.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: The Serengeti's lions and the wildebeest migration.

history.text: Swahili city-states such as Kilwa traded across the Indian Ocean, and Zanzibar later became the centre of an Omani trading empire. Germany colonised the mainland, Tanganyika, which Britain took after the First World War. Tanganyika became independent in 1961 under Julius Nyerere and joined with Zanzibar in 1964 to form Tanzania.

events.title: Omani capital
events.text: The Sultan of Oman moves his court to Zanzibar.

events.title: Maji Maji rebellion
events.text: A major uprising against German rule.

government.text: Tanzania is a presidential republic, a union of the mainland and Zanzibar, which has its own government. The CCM party has governed since independence. Samia Suluhu Hassan became its first female President in 2021. The disputed 2025 election was followed by deadly protests.

economy.text: Tanzania exports gold, cashews, coffee and tobacco. Tourism to Kilimanjaro, Serengeti and Zanzibar is a big earner.

culture.text: Swahili, spoken across East Africa, is Tanzania's national language. Mount Kilimanjaro is Africa's highest mountain, and the Serengeti hosts the great migration. Zanzibar's Stone Town mixes African, Arab, Indian and European influences.

items.title: Serengeti
items.text: Plains crossed by millions of migrating animals.

items.title: Stone Town
items.text: Zanzibar's old trading city, listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Tingatinga painting and bongo flava music.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Tanzania co-hosts the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations with Kenya and Uganda. Filbert Bayi set the 1,500 m world record in 1974.

items.text: Co-hosts the Africa Cup of Nations.

didYouKnow: Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest free-standing mountain in the world.
Freddie Mercury of Queen was born in Zanzibar.

keyPeople.name: Abdulrazak Gurnah
keyPeople.text: Born in Zanzibar; won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2021.
